 This Appeal Coming On For Orders, This Day The
Court Delivered The Following:
 Judgment

Though matter is listed for orders for steps to un-served respondent, as matter was of year 2015,
counsel was heard on merits for disposal of appeal.
2. It was submitted by learned counsel for appellant that appeal was by owner challenging finding of tribunal on negligence.

It was submitted that as per claimant, on 09.02.2012 at 5.30 p.m. when he was riding motorcycle bearing registration no.KA-28/U-7632 from Bagewadi towards Masibinal, an auto rickshaw bearing registration no.KA-28/B-0036 driven by its driver in rash and negligent manner dashed against motorcycle from opposite direction.
In said accident, claimant sustained amputation of right arm.
Despite taking treatment he did not recover fully and filed claim petition under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act against owner.
3. On service of notice, appellant appeared and filed objections denying occurrence of accident and NC: 2023:KHC-K:7366 negligence of driver.
It was also alleged that rider of motorcycle himself was negligent as he had no driving licence to ride motorcycle.
4. Based on pleadings, tribunal framed issues and recorded evidence.
Claimant was examined as PW.1 and Exs.P.1 to P.10 got marked and thereafter matter was posted for judgment and impugned award passed.
5. It was submitted that since accident in question was head-on collision, negligence was required to be apportioned between both vehicles.
On quantum, it was also submitted that though claimant did not examine Doctor, tribunal assessed functional disability at 70% and awarded excessive compensation and sought reduction.

6. Heard learned counsel for parties and perused impugned award.
7.

From above submission and since owner is in challenge on negligence as well as quantum, points that would arise for consideration are :

2 NC: 2023:KHC-K:7366
"(i) Whether finding of tribunal on negligence call for interference?
(ii) Whether compensation requires reduction?"

Point no.(i) :
8.

In order to establish actionable negligence against respondent, claimant produced FIR,
Complaint, Motor Vehicle Inspector's Report, Spot Panchanama and Charge-sheet marked as Exs.P.1 to P.5 respectively.
Same impute negligence against driver of auto rickshaw.
Merely on ground that there was head-on collision, it cannot be presumed that it was due to negligence of both rider of motorcycle and driver of auto rickshaw.
Tribunal applied principle of 'res ipsa loquitur' to conclude entire negligence against auto rickshaw driver.
A categorical finding is recorded that motorcycle was on its left side and auto rickshaw came on wrong side and dashed against motorcycle.
There is no material pointed out to overrule this finding of fact.
Point no.(i) is answered in negative.

NC: 2023:KHC-K:7366 Point no.(ii) :
9.
Admittedly claimant sustained amputation of right arm.
He also sustained fracture of Type IIIA fracture of right femur and tibia with bone loss.
In absence of evidence of Doctor, tribunal has taken recourse to schedule given under Workmen's Compensation Act and attributed loss of functional disability at 70%.

Though on first glance same may appear excessive, however, considering law laid down in case of Erudaya Priya vs. State Express Transport Corporation Limited1, that even in injury cases, claimant would be entitled for addition of future prospects, award would not call for interference.

entities.text: Erudaya Priya vs. State Express Transport Corporation Limited1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
10. Apart from above, tribunal has awarded `1,28,506/- towards 'medical expenses', `10,000/-
towards 'loss of amenities', `18,000/- towards 'loss of income during laid-up period', `10,000/-
towards AIR 2020 SCC 4284 NC: 2023:KHC-K:7366 'incidental expenses' which cannot be under any circumstances be stated to be grossly excessive or unjustified.
Hence, point no.(ii) is also answered in negative.

Consequently, following :
ORDER (i) Appeal is dismissed.
(ii) Amount in deposit is ordered to be transmitted to tribunal for payment.
(iii) Appellant shall deposit balance compensation before tribunal with a period of six weeks from date of receipt of certified copy of this judgment.
